title: Kernel compatibility matrix and interop RFC scrub notes
content:
Meeting: Kernel compatibility matrix & interop RFC scrub
Date: 2025-07-11
Attendees: Aisha Patel (chair), Marco Diaz, Lina Chen, Rajiv Menon, Marta Ivanova, Tom Hsu (observability)
Purpose: Rapid review of the kernel-compatibility draft RFC, surface practical interop constraints across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and land on a deployable short-term plan + medium-term design.

Background / Motivation:
- Recent customer report (INF-2339) surfaced correctness differences when a model artifact built for CUDA-optimized quant kernels is routed to a Dedicated node that only has an older kernel ABI present. Minimal truncation errors turned into subtle tokenization drift in long-conversation regen tests.
- Private customers (air-gapped) sometimes have different libcudnn/libcuda revisions; we need clear semantics for model artifact compatibility and graceful fallback.
- The RFC proposes a "capability bitmap" attached to model artifacts and a runtime adapter that performs capability negotiation at load time.

Summary of discussion:
1) Compatibility semantics and guarantees
   - We agreed to three capability tiers: STRICT (exact kernel match required), COMPAT (compatible alternative kernels allowed), FALLBACK (reference kernels allowed). These map to rollout policies: Hosted defaults to COMPAT for performance; Dedicated supports COMPAT+STRICT per reservation; Private defaults to FALLBACK unless customer configures otherwise.
   - Important invariant: model outputs MUST be bit-reproducible only within STRICT; COMPAT and FALLBACK can diverge in low-magnitude token-prob differences. We will explicitly document expectations and provide a small regression harness (see linked artifacts).

2) Adapter vs ABI layering trade-off
   - Option A: implement an adapter shim in runtime that mediates kernel entry points and performs light emulation for missing ops (fast to ship).
   - Option B: formalize an on-disk ABI with strict versioning and require model packaging to include a kernel-compat manifest (more robust long-term).
   - Decision: Short-term ship adapter shim (Option A) + add ABI manifest to model packaging v2 (Option B) as medium-term milestone. Shim will be opt-in via a runtime flag for Dedicated/Private while Hosted flips it on by default.

3) Quantization format compatibility
   - We enumerated common quant formats (int8/ivec, q4_0, q8_0, float16-fused) and mapped which runtime kernels are known to be compatible. Lina will compile a canonical matrix.
   - We will not allow silent down-conversion of quant formats in COMPAT mode. Down-conversion must be explicit and gated by a quality/regression test.

4) Fallback policy and observable signals
   - Define telemetry: kernel_negotiate.success, kernel_negotiate.fallback_reason, kernel_negotiate.latency_penalty_ms. These should be emitted at load-time and sampled per-session. Tom will add fields to the runtime schema and dashboard.
   - Runtime will emit an event when reference fallback is used and attach a short deterministic hash of input prompt to help debugging while preserving PII constraints.

5) Testing requirements
   - Add model-level artifact tests: unit verify kernel capability bits, CI smoke run for short-sequence generation across kernel variants, and a long-convo regression suite (stochastic seed fixed).
   - Integration matrix in CI must run a 3x3 matrix: {STRICT, COMPAT, FALLBACK} x {CUDA-12, CUDA-11, CPU-only} with a small set of representative models. This will gate model onboarding.

6) Rollout plan
   - Week 0 (short): land adapter shim behind a feature flag, wire telemetry, add unit tests (2 weeks).
   - Week 2: enable shim in Hosted for non-critical traffic (canary), collect delta metrics.
   - Week 4: enable shim for Dedicated opt-in clusters; inform early enterprise customers.
   - Month 2: release model packaging v2 with capability manifest and start rejecting artifacts without manifest in a grace window.

7) Operational playbook excerpts
   - If a model is failing due to missing kernel ops, runtime should: (1) try shim emulation, (2) if still failing, log a specific kernel mismatch alert and fallback to reference kernel if FALLBACK is allowed, (3) if no fallback allowed, mark the model as UNSERVABLE and surface a clear error with remediation steps in the console.
   - Console error page should link to the "kernel capability quick fix" runbook (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Performance regressions from shim emulation on hot paths: need microbenchmarks. Action: Marco to prototype microbench for top-5 ops (due 2025-07-18).
- Backwards compatibility for artifacts packaged before capability-manifests: plan to generate a best-effort manifest at onboarding time but we must not silently change behavior for existing customers.
- Legal/compliance: In Private/on-prem, enabling telemetry is sensitive. We will add a telemetry opt-in knob per deployment (product/security to sign off).

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Lina: Produce canonical kernel x quant-format compatibility matrix (spreadsheet) and upload to Confluence. Due 2025-07-16.
- Marco: Microbenchmark shim emulation cost for top-5 ops; include CPU and GPU profiles. Due 2025-07-18.
- Rajiv: Draft model-packaging v2 schema (capability bitmap + optional fallback policy). PR to runtime repo. Due 2025-07-25.
- Marta: Update onboarding CI to include the 3x3 compatibility matrix (initial run with smoke models). Due 2025-07-21.
- Tom: Add telemetry fields and dashboard panels for kernel negotiation events. Due 2025-07-20.
- Aisha: Draft customer-facing note for Dedicated/Private customers describing compatibility expectations and the rollout schedule. Due 2025-07-22.

Decisions recorded:
- Ship adapter shim (short-term) and design ABI/manifest for model packaging v2 (medium-term).
- Define three capability tiers (STRICT/COMPAT/FALLBACK) and document expectations per deployment type.
- No silent quant-format conversions in COMPAT mode.

Follow-ups / next meeting:
- Weekly sync to review Lina/Marco prototypes and CI results. Next sync: 2025-07-18 10:00 PDT.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please reference the Confluence matrix before commenting on the manifest schema; the matrix will influence which capability bits are required vs optional.
- If you manage a customer/private deployment, flag any telemetry/legal constraints in the PR for model-packaging v2.

Appendix (useful links):
- Runtime PR with initial shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/456
- Customer incident: JIRA-INF-2339 (long-convo drift report)
- Suggested regression harness: s3://redwood-artifacts/model-kernel-regression-harness/

End of notes.
